sources.title: USSR Law No. 1360-I, 14 March 1990: creation of the Presidency and constitutional amendments
sources.publisher: USSR Congress of People's Deputies; original law held by GARF, reproduced by Bavarian State Library, 1000 Schluesseldokumente
sources.access_method: Russian original-law transcription read; four GARF facsimile leaves visually inspected

claims.text: The law creates the USSR Presidency; new Article 127 identifies the President as head of the Soviet state.
claims.locator: Section I; Section II.3, Article 127; facsimile pages 1 and 3

claims.text: The law removes the preamble's leading-party sentence and replaces Article 6 with participation by the CPSU, other parties, organizations and movements.
claims.locator: Section II.1-2, Article 6; facsimile page 1
claims.uncertainty: Replacement of wording is not dissolution of the CPSU or proof that every political organization was registered.

claims.text: The first President is elected by the USSR Congress for five years and enters office upon taking the oath; this differs from the new general popular-election rule.
claims.locator: Section III.1-2; Article 127.1; facsimile pages 3 and 14
claims.uncertainty: A statutory selection rule, not evidence of who was elected or when an oath was taken.

claims.text: The dated signature block identifies M. Gorbachev as Chairman of the USSR Supreme Soviet.
claims.locator: Signature and date block; facsimile page 14
claims.uncertainty: One signed office observation; neither a complete chairmanship nor a presidential appointment.

claims.text: Section IV makes the law effective upon adoption. The instrument is dated 14 March 1990 and numbered 1360-I.
claims.locator: Section IV and instrument number/date; facsimile page 14
claims.uncertainty: No later constitutional version or office lifespan is certified by this enactment.

sources.scope_note: Claims use the reproduced primary Russian law, not the separate 2011/2024 scholarly introduction or its political interpretations. The repository cites GARF F. R-9654, Op. 1, D. 121, leaves 22-35 and the 1990 third extraordinary Congress stenographic report, volume 3, pages 192-207. Only facsimile pages 1, 3, 13 and 14 were visually reviewed. The 14 March law date must not become Gorbachev's presidential oath date.

sources.title: Diplomatic Bluebook 1990, Section 4: Soviet Union
sources.access_method: Official HTML text read through web retrieval; separate direct HTTP download returned 403 and was not accepted as source bytes

claims.text: Japan's 1990 diplomatic account reports Gorbachev's election as General Secretary at the July 1990 CPSU congress while separately calling him President.
claims.locator: 1. Internal Politics, (1) Progress in Political Reform, July congress paragraphs
claims.uncertainty: Month-level contemporaneous diplomatic observation; original CPSU election protocol and exact election day were not inspected.

claims.text: The account reports a new Deputy General Secretary office supporting the General Secretary and supervising the Secretariat, with Vladimir Ivashkov elected.
claims.locator: 1. Internal Politics, (1) Progress in Political Reform, last paragraph
claims.uncertainty: The source spells the name Ivashkov; reconciliation with original-language identity and election records is pending. This is not a succession entitlement or a continuous deputy term.

sources.scope_note: A primary record of Japan's contemporary diplomatic reporting, not an original Soviet party register or election instrument. Retain its month precision and the reported Ivashkov spelling. No independent use is made of its shorthand for constitutional powers, its labels for new groups, or its republic-level office descriptions. The edition year is not a known website publication day.

sources.title: Letter from President Bush to Soviet President Gorbachev, 20 March 1990 (FRUS 1989-1992, volume XXXI, document 90)
sources.publisher: United States Department of State, Office of the Historian; George H. W. Bush Presidential Library record
sources.access_method: Official archival diplomatic-letter transcription and source notes read

claims.text: Bush's letter dated 20 March 1990 addresses Gorbachev as President; the editorial transmission note identifies him as USSR President.
claims.locator: Document heading, dated salutation and footnote 3
claims.uncertainty: An office observation in diplomatic correspondence, not the election, oath, term start or proof of continuous service.

sources.title: UN General Assembly document A/46/771 (13 December 1991): letter of 12 December 1991 from Belarus transmitting the Minsk Declaration and the Agreement establishing the Commonwealth of Independent States of 8 December 1991
sources.publisher: United Nations, General Assembly (circulated at the request of Belarus; English translation of a Russian original)

claims.text: Annex I: the leaders of the Republic of Belarus, the RSFSR and Ukraine proclaim the establishment of the Commonwealth of Independent States; signed S. Shushkevich (Chairman of the Supreme Soviet of the Republic of Belarus), B. Yeltsin (President of the RSFSR) and L. Kravchuk (President of Ukraine), Minsk, 8 December 1991.
claims.locator: PDF page 2, Annex I and signature block
claims.uncertainty: A political declaration in UN English translation. The office titles are signature observations only and are not used as holder observations.

claims.text: Annex II, preamble: the Republic of Belarus, the Russian Federation (RSFSR) and Ukraine, as founder states of the USSR and signatories of the Union Treaty of 1922, declare that the USSR as a subject of international law and a geopolitical reality no longer exists; Article 1 establishes the Commonwealth of Independent States.
claims.locator: PDF page 3, preamble and Article 1
claims.uncertainty: A statement by three republics, not an act of a USSR organ, and it does not end the USSR Presidency. The English 'no longer exists' renders the Russian present tense 'прекращает свое существование' ('ceases its existence'), shown by the GARF copy (su_garf_belovezha_copy_19911208). Signature is not entry into force.

claims.text: Article 11: from the moment of signature, the laws of third states, including the former USSR, may not be applied in the signatories' territories. Article 14: Minsk is the official seat of the coordinating bodies, and the activity of bodies of the former USSR in the territories of member states ceases. Done at Minsk, 8 December 1991; signed for the RSFSR by B. Yeltsin and G. Burbulis.
claims.locator: PDF page 6, Articles 11-14 and signature block
claims.uncertainty: Signature date only. Under the Alma-Ata Protocol of 21 December the Agreement enters into force for each party on ratification. The RSFSR ratified it on 12 December 1991 (su_rsfsr_minsk_ratification_19911212); point 2 of that ratification qualifies Article 11 by applying former-USSR norms in the RSFSR, until RSFSR legislation is adopted, insofar as they do not contradict the RSFSR Constitution, RSFSR legislation and the Agreement. The Belarus and Ukraine ratifications were not reviewed.

sources.scope_note: UN English translation of a Russian original, circulated on 13 December 1991 at the request of Belarus under a covering letter dated 12 December 1991 from its Permanent Representative. Circulation and transmission are neither signature nor ratification. Scanned PDF with an OCR layer.

sources.title: Rosarkhiv virtual exhibition item 10-12: Agreement on the creation of the Commonwealth of Independent States, 8 December 1991 (GARF photocopy with autograph signatures)
sources.publisher: Federal Archival Agency (Rosarkhiv), 2012 virtual exhibition; record held by GARF, F. 10026, Op. 4, D. 1303, L. 1-5

claims.text: GARF holds a photocopy with the autograph signatures of S. Shushkevich and V. Kebich (Republic of Belarus), B. Yeltsin and G. Burbulis (RSFSR) and L. Kravchuk and V. Fokin (Ukraine). Its Russian preamble states that the USSR as a subject of international law and a geopolitical reality 'прекращает свое существование' (ceases its existence); leaf 5 carries Articles 11-14 and 'Совершено в городе Минске 8 декабря 1991 года'.
claims.locator: Exhibit caption; facsimile leaves 1 and 5
claims.uncertainty: Rosarkhiv calls it a photocopy ('ксерокопия') with autographs, not an authentic signed copy; the authentic copies were not reviewed. It records signature, not ratification or entry into force.

sources.scope_note: The 2012 exhibition page (caption and transcription) and facsimile leaves 1 and 5, read from Internet Archive captures because the official host refused connections. Leaf 4 was downloaded but not relied on.

sources.title: Resolution of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet No. 2014-I of 12 December 1991 'On ratification of the Agreement on the creation of the Commonwealth of Independent States' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii' of the State System of Legal Information; the portal card cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RSFSR i Verkhovnogo Soveta RSFSR 1991 No. 51, art. 1798

claims.text: Citing point 15 of Article 109 of the RSFSR Constitution, the RSFSR Supreme Soviet ratifies the Agreement between the Republic of Belarus, the Russian Federation (RSFSR) and Ukraine on the creation of the Commonwealth of Independent States, signed at Minsk on 8 December 1991 (point 1). To give effect to Article 11 of the Agreement, it provides that until the corresponding RSFSR laws are adopted, norms of the former USSR apply in the RSFSR insofar as they do not contradict the RSFSR Constitution, RSFSR legislation and the Agreement (point 2). Signed R. I. Khasbulatov, Chairman of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet, Moscow, House of Soviets of the RSFSR, 12 December 1991, No. 2014-I.
claims.locator: Preamble, points 1-3; signature and date block
claims.uncertainty: Ratification by one party, the RSFSR, on 12 December, separate from the 8 December signature. The resolution gives no entry-into-force date of its own and no date of deposit or notification; the Alma-Ata Protocol's rule that the Agreement enters into force for each party on ratification was signed later, on 21 December. The Belarus and Ukraine ratifications were not reviewed. An act of an RSFSR body, not of a USSR organ.

sources.scope_note: RSFSR ratification of the Minsk Agreement, filed in this packet because it dates the Agreement's effect for one party and qualifies Article 11. Gazette citation: Vedomosti 1991 No. 51, art. 1798. The portal text prints the republic's name without 'Soviet' in its preamble ('Российской Федеративной Социалистической Республики'); the signed original reads the full name.

sources.title: Rosarkhiv virtual exhibition item 10-03: Resolution of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet 'On ratification of the Agreement on the creation of the Commonwealth of Independent States', 12 December 1991 (GARF original)
sources.publisher: Federal Archival Agency (Rosarkhiv), 2012 virtual exhibition; original held by GARF, F. 10026, Op. 1, D. 576, L. 175

claims.text: Rosarkhiv describes the item as the typescript original with the autograph signature of R. I. Khasbulatov, Chairman of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet (GARF F. 10026, Op. 1, D. 576, L. 175). The facsimile shows points 1-3 as in the portal text and 'Москва, Дом Советов РСФСР, 12 декабря 1991 года, № 2014-I'.
claims.locator: Exhibit caption; facsimile image (folio 175)
claims.uncertainty: Corroborates the ratification date and text; it is not an instrument of deposit and gives no entry-into-force date.

sources.scope_note: The 2012 exhibition page (caption and transcription) and the facsimile of the signed original, read from Internet Archive captures because the official host refused connections. The facsimile was viewed at full size.

sources.title: UN document A/47/60-S/23329 (30 December 1991): letter of 27 December 1991 from Belarus transmitting the Alma-Ata Protocol, Declaration and related decisions of 21 December 1991
sources.publisher: United Nations, General Assembly and Security Council (circulated at the request of Belarus; English translation of Russian originals; the Russian-language issue of the same symbol was also read)

claims.text: Annex I, the Protocol to the Minsk Agreement: the Republic of Azerbaijan, the Republic of Armenia, the Republic of Belarus, the Republic of Kazakhstan, the Republic of Kyrgyzstan, the Republic of Moldova, the Russian Federation (RSFSR), the Republic of Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, the Republic of Uzbekistan and Ukraine constitute the Commonwealth of Independent States as High Contracting Parties. The Agreement establishing the Commonwealth enters into force for each party from the moment of its ratification, and documents regulating cooperation are to be drawn up taking into account the reservations made on ratification. Signed for the Russian Federation (RSFSR) by B. Yeltsin, Alma-Ata, 21 December 1991.
claims.locator: English PDF page 3, Annex I
claims.uncertainty: Georgia is not a signatory. The ratification rule is dated 21 December, after the RSFSR's ratification of 12 December. The other parties' ratification dates were not reviewed.

claims.text: Annex II, the Alma-Ata Declaration: the Commonwealth is neither a state nor a supra-state entity. The UN English text reads 'With the establishment of the Commonwealth of Independent States, the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics ceased to exist'; the Russian-language issue reads 'С образованием Содружества Независимых Государств Союз Советских Социалистических Республик прекращает свое существование' (present tense). The participants guarantee the discharge of the former USSR's treaty obligations. Signed by the same eleven leaders, Yeltsin as 'Президент Российской Федерации (РСФСР)', Alma-Ata, 21 December 1991.
claims.locator: English PDF pages 4-5, Annex II; Russian-language issue, PDF page 5
claims.uncertainty: A multilateral declaration, not an act of a USSR organ. The English past tense is not used to date the end of the USSR or of any USSR office; the Russian text is in the present tense. No text addresses the USSR Presidency or Gorbachev.

claims.text: Annex IV: a Council of Heads of State is established as the supreme organ of the Commonwealth, together with a Council of Heads of Government; plenipotentiaries are to submit by 30 December 1991 proposals on abolishing the structures of the former USSR and on the Commonwealth's coordinating bodies.
claims.locator: English PDF page 7, Annex IV
claims.uncertainty: An instruction to propose abolition, not the abolition of any named USSR office.

sources.scope_note: UN English translation of Russian originals, circulated on 30 December 1991 under a covering letter dated 27 December 1991 from the Permanent Representative of Belarus; transmission is not signature. The English PDF is an OCR-reconstructed rendering with visible recognition errors. Annex III (interim command of the armed forces assigned to Marshal E. I. Shaposhnikov) and Annex V (support for Russia's continuance of the USSR's membership of the UN and other international organizations) were verified but are not imported: they concern no institution in this packet, and continuity of UN membership is not a domestic institutional mapping.

sources.title: Memorandum of telephone conversation: telcon with Mikhail Gorbachev, President of the Soviet Union, 25 December 1991, 10:03-10:25 a.m., Camp David
sources.publisher: US National Archives (NARA) catalog copy; George H. W. Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Presidential Telcon Files, OA/ID CF01730, folder CF01730-013

claims.text: The White House memorandum identifies the other party to a call on 25 December 1991, 10:03-10:25 a.m., at Camp David, as 'Mikhail Gorbachev, President of the Soviet Union'; interpreter Dmitri Zarechnak, notetaker Nicholas Burns of the NSC staff.
claims.locator: PDF page 1, subject, participants and date lines
claims.uncertainty: A US record; the times are the US side's and no time zone is printed. An office observation, not a term.

claims.text: Gorbachev says he had considered making his statement on Tuesday or that day and decided to make it that day, at the end of the day; in about two hours he will speak on Moscow TV with a short statement about his decision.
claims.locator: PDF page 1, second and third Gorbachev paragraphs
claims.uncertainty: A stated intention before the broadcast, in a translated memorandum rather than a verbatim transcript.

claims.text: Gorbachev says he has on his desk a decree of the President of the USSR on his resignation; he will also resign his duties as Commander-in-Chief and transfer authority to use nuclear weapons to the President of the Russian Federation, and as soon as he announces his resignation he will put these decrees into effect. Bush later notes that the constitutional responsibilities on this issue have been passed to Boris Yeltsin.
claims.locator: PDF page 2, paragraph beginning 'Now, about Russia'; PDF page 3, first paragraph
claims.uncertainty: A report of intent, not the instruments. Whether a decree on resignation existed separately from decree UP-3162 is not established. The transfer of nuclear-use authority to the President of the Russian Federation is not an institutional succession from the USSR Presidency.

sources.scope_note: Declassified on 23 September 2008 (stamp: E.O. 12958 as amended, 2004-1975-MR). Scanned PDF; page 4 is the library's citation sheet, not a textual record. The bush41library.tamu.edu copy redirected to a homepage and was not used.

sources.title: Address to the Nation on the Commonwealth of Independent States, 25 December 1991 (Public Papers of the Presidents)
sources.publisher: George H.W. Bush Presidential Library and Museum (NARA), Public Papers of the Presidents

claims.text: Speaking at 9 p.m. from the Oval Office, Bush says that the formation of the Commonwealth of Independent States 'marks the end of the old Soviet Union, signified today by Mikhail Gorbachev's decision to resign as President', and that he spoke with Gorbachev that morning.
claims.locator: Paragraphs 5-6 and closing note
claims.uncertainty: A foreign head of state's characterization after the event: it reports a decision to resign that day, not an instrument or an effective moment.

sources.scope_note: Paragraphs are counted from 'Good evening'. The recognition paragraphs ('First', 'Second', 'Third': recognition of Russia led by President Yeltsin, support for Russia's assumption of the USSR's Security Council seat, and recognition of the other former republics) were verified but are not imported: diplomatic recognition is not a succession of any USSR domestic office.

lifecycle.note: The law creates the USSR Presidency on 14 March 1990. Later constitutional changes and the ending of the institution remain unresolved; this date is not a person's appointment or oath.

holder_claims.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
holder_claims.note: Office observation: the US memorandum of the call of 25 December 1991 names him President of the Soviet Union. His announced cessation that day is recorded in separate role claims (su_telcon_resignation_decrees_19911225, su_bush_address_resign_19911225).
holder_claims.uncertainty: SURU-TR91-06: no Soviet instrument or effective moment has been accepted, so no until is set; the 25 December announcement is a dated claim, not a term boundary. The 1990 election and oath remain unsourced.

unresolved: Obtain the election result and oath record separately from the law creating the post; 14 March enactment is not a personal appointment.
Review later 1990-1991 amendments, vice presidency, acting authority, resignation and abolition without projecting the March text through dissolution.
Holding this state office does not establish party leadership or transfer authority to a post-USSR state.

SURU-TR91-06: Gorbachev's cessation is accepted only as an announcement on 25 December 1991, from two US records (the NARA telcon and the Bush address). A Soviet primary text of the address, decree UP-3162 from an official host or facsimile, any separate decree on resignation and the effective moment remain open; no holder until is set.

SURU-TR91-07: no reviewed instrument abolishes the USSR Presidency or amends Article 127. The Minsk statement (8 December, three republics), the Alma-Ata Declaration (21 December; the Russian text reads 'прекращает свое существование', present tense) and the Council of Republics declaration of 26 December (known only from a non-official transcription) are competing candidates; lifecycle.until stays null.

SURU-TR91-04/05: under the Alma-Ata Protocol the Minsk Agreement binds each party from ratification; only the RSFSR ratification (12 December 1991, 2014-I) is reviewed, and the Belarus and Ukraine ratifications are open. None of these CIS acts is an act of a USSR organ, and none maps this office to the RSFSR or Russian presidency.

unresolved: Separate this chairmanship from the earlier Chairman of the Presidium title; the signature proves neither term start nor end.
Obtain the later chairman election and full chamber membership records independently.

SURU-TR91-08: Declaration 142-N of the Council of Republics (26 December 1991) and order 141-N of the Council of the Union chairman are known only from a non-official transcription of Vedomosti VS SSSR 1991 No. 52. They are leads, not claims, and change no lifecycle; they would be acts of single chambers, not of the whole Supreme Soviet.
This is a bounded 1990-1991 source inventory: one party and three state institutions, not an exhaustive USSR party, faction, opposition, republic or coalition census.

The packet does not establish absence of other organizations. Discover original party registers, congresses, candidate organizations and opposition movements with separate union/republic jurisdiction.
Exact party election dates, acting roles, original spelling and full leadership intervals remain unresolved; contemporary Japanese diplomatic reporting is not an original CPSU election protocol.
1991 office changes, emergency claims, resignations, suspensions and dissolution require their own source review. No legal or organizational continuity through 2026 is inferred.
The USSR packet remains separate from Russia. Existing game party mappings, historical avatar eligibility, likeness approval and post-cutoff fictional succession are not changed.

CLAUDE-C01-05 reviews only the December 1991 records bearing on the Presidency (SURU-TR91-04 to 08). The August 1991 events, the CPSU suspension and the September 1991 changes to the Congress and Supreme Soviet remain unreviewed.
